# PlotNado

PlotNado builds genome browser-style figures from Python code or editable YAML templates.
It is useful when you need reproducible plots for BigWig-like signals, intervals, peaks,
links, genes, and optional matrix-style genomic data.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Start with [Installation](docs/installation.qmd) if you are setting up the project,
or [Quick Start](docs/quickstart.qmd) if you already have the uv environment.
:::

## First figure

```{python}
from docs._examples import REGION, quickstart_figure

quickstart_figure().plot(REGION)
```

The example is rendered by Quarto from deterministic in-memory data. The same pattern
is used throughout the docs so code and output stay in sync.

## Two workflows

### Python API

```python
from plotnado import GenomicFigure

fig = (
    GenomicFigure()
    .scalebar()
    .axis()
    .bigwig(signal, title="Signal", style="fill")
    .bed(intervals, title="Intervals", display="expanded")
)
fig.save("plot.png", region="chr1:1,010,000-1,080,000")
```

Use this route in scripts, notebooks, analysis pipelines, and executable docs.

### CLI + YAML

```bash
uv run plotnado init sample1.bw peaks.narrowpeak --auto --output template.yaml
uv run plotnado validate template.yaml
uv run plotnado plot template.yaml --region chr1:1,000,000-1,100,000 --output plot.png
```

Use this route when the figure definition should be reviewed or versioned as a
human-editable YAML file.
